B01.title: Analysis of Dynamic Five-Element Model
B01.access: Author-uploaded paper, equations inspected; proceedings contents checked
B01.why: Closest bilinear five-element predecessor. Its six-term model must be mapped by coefficients and offsets, rather than identified with DM.

B02.authors: Haipeng Lin; Wenxin Shi; Jing Han
B02.title: Analysis of Enzymatic Regulatory Five-Element Model
B02.access: Metadata and citation chain; main text unavailable
B02.why: Highest-priority outstanding equation and theorem check. The title does not establish the denominator convention.

B03.authors: Haipeng Lin; Wenxin Shi; Jing Han
B03.title: Comparison of Enzymatic Regulatory Network Topologies
B03.access: Metadata; purported online full text has version mismatch
B03.why: Do not attribute the later journal manuscript attached to a proceedings record to this 2022 paper without inspecting its actual PDF.

B04.title: Comparison of Multi-Node Networks on Biological Properties
B04.access: Metadata verified through Crossref; main text unavailable
B04.why: Could contain the intermediate generalization beyond five nodes. Priority remains unresolved at theorem level.

B05.title: What is special of “five” in biological regulatory networks?
B05.access: Publisher abstract/references; partial author-manuscript equation; public supplement source inspected
B05.why: Essential exact-model comparison. The supplement confirms a Hopf parameter-space study and analytical adaptation arguments; a numerical-only characterization would be inaccurate.

B06.title: Discovering golden ratio in the world’s first five-agent network in ancient China
B06.why: Directly defeats novelty based merely on golden-ratio constants in a five-element network. The model and stability claim differ from DM.

B07.authors: P. Bellavite; M. Semizzi; S. Lussignoli; G. Andrioli; U. Bartocci
B07.title: A computer model of the ‘five elements’ theory of traditional Chinese medicine
B07.why: Older computational five-element network precedent. It establishes historical context, not an exact DM theorem.

B08.authors: Dirk L. van Kekem; Alef E. Sterk
B08.title: Travelling waves and their bifurcations in the Lorenz-96 model
B08.access: Full arXiv paper inspected: Lemma 1, Theorems 2/4, Propositions 5/6, §4.3
B08.why: Principal comparison for quadratic cosine dispersion, finite-size Hopf selection, and nonlinear criticality.

B09.authors: Dirk L. van Kekem; Alef E. Sterk
B09.title: Wave propagation in the Lorenz-96 model
B09.access: Full article available; wave and size discussion inspected
B09.why: Companion precedent for travelling-wave interpretation and large-size wavelength/period behavior.

B10.authors: Dirk L. van Kekem; Alef E. Sterk
B10.title: Symmetries in the Lorenz-96 Model
B10.venue: International Journal of Bifurcation and Chaos 29, 1950008
B10.why: Symmetry and symmetry-breaking steady-state precedent; do not conflate it with the separate Wave propagation article.

B11.title: On the Lorenz ’96 model and some generalizations
B11.venue: Discrete and Continuous Dynamical Systems – B 27(2), 769–797; online 2021
B11.access: Full arXiv v2 inspected: Lemma 1, Eq. (29), Appendix A
B11.why: Especially close prior for Fourier-based first-Lyapunov reduction in cyclic quadratic systems.

B12.title: Hopf Bifurcation and Phase Patterns in Symmetric Ring Networks
B12.venue: arXiv preprint; no journal version verified
B12.access: Full v1 HTML inspected: Theorems 3.7, 5.5, 5.7 and Corollary 5.6
B12.why: Direct modern source for ring phase patterns, unrestricted ordering, and direction. Sparse positive DM coefficients impose additional restrictions.

B13.title: Hopf Bifurcation in Asymmetric Ring Networks: Constraints on Phase Shifts
B13.venue: arXiv preprint; no journal version verified
B13.why: Generic ring nondegeneracy is background, not a substitute for a derivative on the designated DM parameter path. Included only for this narrow comparison.

B14.authors: Ian Stewart; Martin Golubitsky; Marcus Pivato
B14.title: Symmetry Groupoids and Patterns of Synchrony in Coupled Cell Networks
B14.venue: SIAM Journal on Applied Dynamical Systems 2(4), 609–646
B14.why: General coupled-cell synchrony theory. Full synchrony of this homogeneous ring is a basic special case.

B15.authors: Martin Golubitsky; Ian Stewart; Andrei Török
B15.title: Patterns of Synchrony in Coupled Cell Networks with Multiple Arrows
B15.venue: SIAM Journal on Applied Dynamical Systems 4(1), 78–100
B15.why: Multiarrow framework is pertinent when modular offsets coincide; quotient and synchrony arguments are established machinery.

B16.title: Hopf Bifurcation in the Presence of Symmetry
B16.venue: Archive for Rational Mechanics and Analysis 87, 107–165
B16.access: Publisher metadata/abstract; theorem also checked through B12
B16.why: Foundational equivariant Hopf reference. A similarly titled 1984 announcement is a separate publication.

B17.title: Toeplitz and Circulant Matrices: A Review
B17.venue: Foundations and Trends in Communications and Information Theory 2(3), 155–239
B17.why: Accessible source for the circulant eigenbasis and unitary diagonalization used throughout P03–P04.

B18.title: Global Stability in Many-Species Systems
B18.access: Publisher metadata/abstract; classical Lyapunov criterion independently specialized here
B18.why: The appropriate foundation for the bilinear model’s diagonal-stability/entropy argument, not a new general stability technique.

B19.authors: J. C. Wildenberg; J. A. Vano; J. C. Sprott
B19.title: Complex spatiotemporal dynamics in Lotka–Volterra ring systems
B19.why: Close ecological predecessor for circulant bilinear rings, cosine spectra and Lyapunov stability regions.

B20.title: The Poincaré–Bendixson theorem for monotone cyclic feedback systems
B20.venue: Journal of Dynamics and Differential Equations 2(4), 367–421
B20.access: Publisher record; relevance cross-checked against B25
B20.why: A crucial scope boundary: the generic multi-input DM ring is not automatically a monotone single-loop feedback system.

B21.title: Degradation rate uniformity determines success of oscillations in repressive feedback regulatory networks
B21.venue: Journal of the Royal Society Interface 15, 20180157
B21.access: Full preprint, Eq. (15) and supplementary derivation
B21.why: Nonlinear criticality benchmark: sign information over function/parameter classes is stronger than a single nonzero coefficient.

B22.authors: Olguța Bușe; Alexey Kuznetsov; Rodrigo A. Pérez
B22.title: Existence of Limit Cycles in the Repressilator Equations

B22.access: Author-uploaded full text and author PDF excerpts

B23.authors: Darren Pais; Carlos H. Caicedo-Núñez; Naomi E. Leonard

B27.access: Primary abstract and metadata; main text not obtained

B28.title: Turing patterns in network-organized activator-inhibitor systems
B28.access: Primary preprint available, dispersion framework inspected

B30.access: Publisher abstract and available article preview
